findings.F1: The tested slope is positive but short of the bar. On the plan's 2-day grid it has a day-clustered t of 1.28 (8,995 cases, 1,230 days). Its size is an unusual move of only +0.08 % per case (t 0.42), 0.3 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade. The test used every coin and fold the data holds, so there is no more data to add.
findings.F2: The rebound is concentrated in the first day after the fall. Over the next 1 day, the same regression on the forecast gives a slope of +0.00038 with a day-clustered t of 2.45 (18,028 cases, 2,405 days). The second day alone, on the 2-day grid, has a slope of -0.00012 (t -0.54). This return given back on day 2 is what dilutes the plan's 2-day measure to t 1.28.
findings.F3: Over 1 day the effect is graded as the idea says. Mean excess return by forecast quintile, mean forecast in brackets:
findings.F4: Over 1 day the effect is broad, not carried by one part of the data.
findings.F5: Neither the coin's 30-day trend nor longer horizons separate the effect.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, measured against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A dip buyer should take the rebound after an unusually large fall for the coin within the following day and not hold for a second day, since the second day gives part of it back and only the most unusual falls clear the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: unusual falls rebound next day
